newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks WTO to postpone Helms-Burton panel.
newsitem.headline: EU asks WTO to postpone Helms-Burton panel.

text.p: The European Union Wednesday asked World Trade Organisation chief Renato Ruggiero to postpone naming a panel to rule on complaints that Washington's Helms-Burton Act contravenes world trade rules.
European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said in a statement that he had asked Ruggeiro to delay naming the panel until Feb. 20 in an attempt to reach a settlement with Washington.
"The European Union is as eager as the United States to resolve the dispute over the Helms-Burton Act," Brittan said. "The EU does not want litigation for its own sake.
The EU and Washington have been at odds for nearly a year over the act, an amalgamation of years of U.S. anti-Cuba policy.

Among other things, the act allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreign individuals or companies benefiting from investments in property confiscated by Havana since the communist revolution of 1959.
This part was suspended by President Clinton in January, but the EU nevertheless proceeded with a complaint at the WTO.
But the EU and Washington have been unable to agree on the composition of the panel and last week Brittan called for Ruggiero to intervene.

Washington has said that the issue was not for the WTO as it involved U.S. national security issues and has threatened to ignore any WTO ruling on the matter -- a move analysts say could seriously undermine the two-year-old Geneva-based WTO.
But Brittan said Washington's claim was "not credible."
Nevertheless, he said, he would ask Ruggiero to delay naming the panel to give time for further discussions with Washington.
